title: Free Cash-on-Cash Return Calculator for Rental Property
headline: Cash-on-Cash Return Calculator for Rental Property
desc: Free, no-signup cash-on-cash return calculator for rental property investors. Estimate annual cash flow and return on cash invested. Nothing is uploaded.
lead: Estimate the cash-on-cash return on a rental property from your own numbers. No account, no upload, no email.
method: Cash-on-cash return divides annual before-tax cash flow (rental income minus operating expenses and mortgage payments) by the total cash you put into the deal (down payment plus closing and rehab costs). It is a simple snapshot and does not account for appreciation, taxes, or the time value of money.
faq: What is a good cash-on-cash return?
There is no universal benchmark. Compare against your own required return and the risk of the specific property; different markets and strategies vary widely.
Does this include taxes?
No. This is a before-tax estimate. Your actual result depends on your tax situation and local rules.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is a simplified educational estimate. Verify every figure with a qualified professional and current official sources.

title: Free Mortgage Affordability Calculator by Income
headline: Mortgage Affordability Calculator by Income
desc: Free no-signup mortgage affordability calculator: see an estimated loan amount from your income, debt-to-income ratio and current interest rate. Nothing uploaded.
lead: See roughly how much home loan your income may support at a given debt-to-income ratio and rate. All math happens in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.
method: The estimate multiplies gross monthly income by your chosen debt-to-income percentage, subtracts other monthly debt payments, then converts the remaining housing payment into a loan amount using the standard fixed-rate amortization formula. It is a rough illustration, not an approval or an offer of credit.
faq: Is this a mortgage approval?
No. It is a rough arithmetic illustration. Lenders use their own underwriting, credit, income verification and property rules.
What DTI should I use?
Different lenders and loan programs use different limits. Check current official program guidelines rather than assuming a number.
Does this include taxes and insurance?
No. Property tax, homeowners insurance, HOA dues and mortgage insurance can materially change what you can afford.

title: Free Auto Loan Payment Calculator With Trade-In
headline: Auto Loan Payment Calculator With Trade-In
desc: Free no-signup auto loan payment calculator with trade-in and down payment. Estimate monthly payment and total interest. Nothing is uploaded.
lead: Estimate a monthly car payment from price, down payment, trade-in value, APR and term. Runs entirely on your device.
method: The amount financed is vehicle price minus down payment and trade-in value. The monthly payment uses the standard amortization formula at the entered APR and term. Taxes, fees, add-ons and dealer incentives are not included.
faq: Does this include sales tax and fees?
No. Add your local sales tax, title, registration and dealer fees to see the out-the-door cost.
Will this affect my credit?
No. This calculator runs locally and does not contact any lender or pull your credit.
Is a longer term always cheaper?
Not necessarily. A longer term lowers the monthly payment but can increase total interest.

title: Free Credit Card Payoff Calculator
headline: Credit Card Payoff Calculator
desc: Free no-signup credit card payoff calculator: estimate months to pay off a balance and how a monthly payment changes the timeline. Nothing uploaded.
lead: See roughly how long a fixed monthly payment takes to clear a credit card balance at a given APR. Runs entirely in your browser.
method: Each month interest is added at one-twelfth of the APR, then your fixed payment is applied. If the payment does not cover the monthly interest, the balance will not fall. New purchases, fees and rate changes are not modeled.
faq: What if my payment is too small?
If the payment does not exceed the interest added each month, the balance does not decrease and the result will say so.
Does this assume a fixed rate?
Yes. Promotional or variable rates can change the result substantially.
Is snowball or avalanche better?
It depends on your balances and rates. This tool models a single account only and is not advice.

title: Free Self-Employment Tax Calculator for 1099 Income
headline: Self-Employment Tax Calculator for 1099 Income
desc: Free no-signup self-employment tax calculator for 1099 and freelance income. Estimate Social Security and Medicare tax. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Estimate US self-employment (SECA) tax on net freelance or 1099 income. You control every input; nothing leaves your device.

metrics.label: Net earnings subject to SE tax (92.35%)

method: Self-employment tax is estimated as 12.4% Social Security on net earnings up to the annual wage base (reduced by other W-2 wages) plus 2.9% Medicare on all net earnings. Net earnings are 92.35% of net profit. The wage base changes each year, so confirm the current figure with the IRS.
faq: Is this my total tax bill?
No. This covers self-employment tax only. Federal and state income tax are separate and are not included.
What is the 92.35% figure?
It is the standard factor used to convert net profit to net earnings subject to self-employment tax.
Can I deduct half of this?
There is a standard deduction for half of self-employment tax on US returns. Confirm current rules with a tax professional or the IRS.

title: Free Hourly to Annual Salary Calculator With Overtime
headline: Hourly to Annual Salary Calculator With Overtime
desc: Free no-signup hourly to annual salary calculator including overtime hours. Convert an hourly wage to yearly pay. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Convert an hourly rate into estimated annual pay, including overtime hours at time-and-a-half. All math runs locally.
method: Annual pay equals hourly rate times regular weekly hours times weeks worked, plus overtime hours paid at 1.5 times the hourly rate. This is gross pay before taxes and deductions, and assumes overtime rules apply to the entered hours.
faq: Is this take-home pay?
No. This is gross pay before tax, insurance and other deductions.
Does everyone get time-and-a-half?
Overtime eligibility depends on local law and your role. Check your jurisdiction and employer policy.
What about unpaid weeks?
Set the weeks-worked field to reflect unpaid time off.

title: Free Freelance Day Rate Calculator
headline: Freelance Day Rate Calculator
desc: Free no-signup freelance day rate calculator: turn a target annual income and billable days into a day rate. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Work backwards from a target income to a day rate using the number of days you can actually bill, plus an expense buffer.
method: The target income is increased by your expense buffer and divided by realistic billable days per year. It does not include tax, and it assumes you can actually bill the entered number of days.
faq: What is a realistic billable-days number?
It varies by role. Count only days you can genuinely invoice after weekends, holidays, admin and time off.
Does this include tax?
No. Set a higher target income or buffer if you need to cover tax.
Should I charge by day or by project?
A day rate is one pricing method. Compare with project or value-based pricing for your market.

title: Free Rental Yield Calculator — Gross and Net
headline: Rental Yield Calculator — Gross and Net
desc: Free no-signup rental yield calculator for gross and net yield on a buy-to-let property. Estimate return from rent and costs. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Estimate gross and net rental yield from purchase price, monthly rent and annual costs. All figures stay on your device.
method: Gross yield is annual rent divided by purchase price. Net yield divides annual rent minus operating expenses by the total cash cost (purchase price plus closing costs). Vacancy, financing and tax are not included.
faq: Which yield should I compare?
Net yield is usually more informative because it includes costs. Compare like with like across properties.
Does this include mortgage costs?
No. This is a property-level yield before financing and tax.
Is a higher yield always better?
Not necessarily. Higher yields can reflect higher risk, lower growth or higher maintenance.

title: Free Personal Loan Payment Calculator
headline: Personal Loan Payment Calculator
desc: Free no-signup personal loan payment calculator: estimate monthly payment, total repaid and total interest. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Estimate a fixed-rate personal loan payment from amount, APR and term. Runs entirely in your browser.
method: The monthly payment uses the standard fixed-rate amortization formula. Origination fees, late fees and variable rates are not included. An estimate is not an offer of credit.
faq: Does this check my eligibility?
No. It only does arithmetic on the numbers you enter and does not contact any lender.
What does APR include?
APR may include certain fees, but it varies by lender. Check the lender disclosure for the exact definition.
Are there fees?
Some loans have origination or early-repayment fees. This tool does not model them.

title: Free Debt-to-Income Ratio Calculator for Mortgage
headline: Debt-to-Income Ratio Calculator for Mortgage
desc: Free no-signup debt-to-income (DTI) calculator for mortgage applicants. Estimate front-end and back-end DTI from income and debts. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Estimate the debt-to-income ratio a lender may look at, using your income, proposed housing payment and other monthly debts.
method: Back-end DTI is total monthly debt payments divided by gross monthly income. Front-end DTI uses only the housing payment. Lenders calculate income and debts using their own rules, which may differ from the figures you enter here.
faq: What DTI do lenders allow?
Limits vary by loan program and lender. Check current official program guidelines.
What counts as monthly debt?
Typically minimum payments on loans and credit cards, but lender definitions vary.
Is this a credit check?
No. Nothing is sent anywhere and no lender is contacted.

title: Free Cap Rate Calculator With Operating Expenses
headline: Cap Rate Calculator With Operating Expenses
desc: Free no-signup cap rate calculator that includes operating expenses and closing costs. Estimate a property-level capitalization rate from your own numbers. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Estimate cap rate from annual rent, operating expenses, purchase price and closing costs. All figures stay on your device.
method: Cap rate here is net operating income (annual rental income minus operating expenses) divided by cost basis (purchase price plus closing costs). Financing, taxes, vacancy and capital expenditures are not included, so this is only a property-level snapshot.
faq: Does cap rate include mortgage payments?
No. Cap rate is a property-level measure before financing. Debt service is looked at separately, for example with DSCR.
Should closing costs be included?
Including them gives a cash-inclusive cap rate. Some investors use only purchase price; compare like with like.
Is this investment advice?
No. It is arithmetic on the numbers you enter. Verify all inputs and assumptions with qualified professionals.

title: Free Monthly Rental Property Cash Flow Calculator
headline: Monthly Rental Property Cash Flow Calculator
desc: Free no-signup monthly rental property cash flow calculator with vacancy and maintenance reserve. Estimate cash flow from your own figures. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Estimate monthly rental cash flow after vacancy, operating costs, mortgage and a maintenance reserve. Nothing leaves your device.
method: Effective rent is monthly rent reduced by your vacancy allowance. Monthly cash flow is effective rent minus operating expenses, mortgage payment and maintenance reserve. Taxes, management fees and one-off repairs are not modeled unless you include them in your expense input.
faq: What should I include in operating expenses?
Typical examples are property tax, insurance, utilities paid by the owner, HOA dues and management. Use figures that match your own situation.
Is this take-home cash?
No. This is a simplified before-tax estimate. Your tax result depends on depreciation, deductions and local rules.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is arithmetic on your inputs. Verify assumptions with a qualified professional.

metrics.label: Maximum new loan at target LTV

faq: Is this an approval?
No. It is arithmetic on your inputs. Lenders use their own underwriting and property rules.
Does this include taxes or cash needed at closing?
No. Add any escrow, prepayment penalty or cash-to-close requirements yourself.
Is refinancing always worthwhile?
Not necessarily. Compare the full cost of the new loan with your current loan and your goals.

title: Free Mortgage Payment Calculator With Taxes, Insurance and HOA
headline: Mortgage Payment Calculator With Taxes, Insurance and HOA
desc: Free no-signup mortgage payment calculator including property tax, homeowners insurance and HOA dues. Estimate a full monthly housing payment. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Estimate principal, interest, property tax, insurance and HOA in one monthly housing figure. Runs locally in your browser.
method: Principal and interest use the standard fixed-rate amortization formula on the loan amount after your down payment. Annual property tax and insurance are divided by twelve and added to monthly HOA dues. Mortgage insurance, PMI and closing costs are not included.
faq: Does this include PMI?
No. If your down payment is below lender thresholds, private mortgage insurance may apply and is not modeled here.
Are taxes and insurance exact?
No. Use your own best estimates. Lenders may escrow and recalculate these amounts.
Is this a loan offer?
No. It is an estimate only, not an approval or offer of credit.

title: Free Quarterly Estimated Tax Calculator for 1099 Income
headline: Quarterly Estimated Tax Calculator for 1099 Income
desc: Free no-signup quarterly estimated tax calculator for 1099 and freelance income. Rough US estimate of self-employment plus income tax. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Roughly estimate a quarterly US estimated-tax payment from net 1099 profit, wages, tax rates and payments already made. Control every input.
method: This rough estimate combines self-employment tax (12.4% Social Security up to the entered wage base, reduced by W-2 wages, plus 2.9% Medicare on 92.35% of net profit) with a simple flat-rate income-tax estimate, subtracts tax already paid, then divides by four. It ignores deductions, credits, QBI, brackets, withholding, state-specific rules and safe-harbor calculations.
faq: Is this my actual required payment?
No. It is a rough illustration only. Use the official IRS estimator or a qualified tax professional for real filing decisions.
Does it include deductions and credits?
No. Standard/itemized deductions, QBI, retirement contributions and credits are not modeled.
What if my income varies?
Quarterly calculations often depend on annualized income. Check current official rules.

title: Free Compound Interest Calculator With Monthly Contributions
headline: Compound Interest Calculator With Monthly Contributions
desc: Free no-signup compound interest calculator with monthly contributions. Estimate future value from an initial amount, monthly addition, rate and time. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Estimate future value with monthly compounding and regular monthly contributions. All math runs in your browser.
method: The starting balance compounds monthly. Each monthly contribution is added at the end of the month and then compounds in later months. The result is before tax, fees and inflation, and assumes the entered rate stays constant.
faq: Are returns guaranteed?
No. A fixed rate is an assumption, not a promise. Actual returns vary and can be negative.
Does this include fees or tax?
No. Subtract your own fees and consider taxes separately.
When are contributions added?
This model adds them at the end of each month.

title: Free Emergency Fund Calculator by Monthly Expenses
headline: Emergency Fund Calculator by Monthly Expenses
desc: Free no-signup emergency fund calculator. See a target fund from essential monthly expenses and the monthly saving needed to reach it. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Set an emergency-fund target from essential monthly expenses and see roughly what you would need to set aside each month. Runs locally.

inputs.label: Months you want to save over

method: The target is essential monthly expenses multiplied by the number of months you want to cover. The monthly saving figure is the remaining gap divided by your chosen number of months. It assumes no interest and no changes in expenses or income.
faq: How many months should I target?
It depends on your job stability, dependents and other resources. Six months is a common illustration, not a rule.
Should I count all expenses?
Use essential expenses you would still need if income stopped, not discretionary spending.
Is this financial advice?
No. It is simple arithmetic on your inputs. Consider your own circumstances and get professional advice where needed.

title: Free Freelance Hourly Rate Calculator With Expenses and Tax Buffer
headline: Freelance Hourly Rate Calculator With Expenses and Tax Buffer
desc: Free no-signup freelance hourly rate calculator with expense and tax buffers. Turn a target income and realistic billable hours into an hourly rate. Nothing uploaded.
lead: Work backwards from a target annual income to an hourly rate using realistic billable hours plus expense and tax buffers. Runs locally.
method: The target take-home income is increased by your expense and tax buffers, then divided by realistic annual billable hours. The buffers are simple percentages you choose, not a tax calculation. Market demand and the value of your work also affect what clients will pay.
faq: Are the buffers tax advice?
No. They are placeholders you set yourself. Confirm your real tax position with a qualified professional.
How many billable hours are realistic?
Count only hours you can genuinely invoice after admin, marketing, holidays and time off.
Does this guarantee clients will pay the rate?
No. It is a pricing input, not a promise about demand or income.
